summary: Researched the books extension's first write-time guard: re-confirmed every deploy-pipeline claim in the dispatch (exact-matcher merge semantics, install-once settings.json, hooks-category execute-bit copy, both rejected email/lean precedents) directly in merge.lua/loader.lua, confirmed the task's file_scope already locks the settings-fragment naming question the dispatch left open, and settled the predicate's parsing shape (tool_name branch, cwd-relative path resolution via git rev-parse --show-toplevel, byte-string prefix/suffix tests with no line-splitting).

artifacts.summary: Research report confirming deploy-pipeline mechanics, resolving the settings-fragment naming question via the locked file_scope, and specifying the predicate's parsing/path-resolution design for the plan phase.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension deploy pipeline (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua), a hook-event array under settings (e.g. .hooks.PreToolUse) is merged by EXACT STRING EQUALITY on the `matcher` field, not by whole-block deep-equal. Registering a new hook under a matcher spelled differently from an existing block (different pipe order, extra tool name, different spacing) creates a second, independently-tracked matcher block rather than joining the existing one -- and the merge is add-only, so a wrong spelling can never be healed by a later redeploy. Always copy the literal existing matcher string byte-for-byte when adding a hook to a shared event (e.g. core's "Write|Edit" block) rather than retyping it.

Across this repo's non-core extensions with a merge_targets.settings entry, the source filename is uniformly settings-fragment.json at the extension root and the target is uniformly .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored, per-clone). Only core deviates: merge-sources/settings-hooks.json targeting the tracked .claude/settings.json, reserved per core's own manifest _comment for "required core functionality rather than personal MCP/permission preference." Any new extension hook needing a durable, tracked, repo-shared registration (not a personal preference) should target .claude/settings.json like core, not copy the settings.local.json convention from email/lean/nix -- those two also happen to be the only existing extension-hook-registration precedents, and both are documented-wrong (email wraps its hook to silently swallow the block exit code; lean never puts the hook key in its fragment at all, so the hook ships unregistered).

In this repo's PreToolUse hook family, the top-level `.cwd` field of the hook's stdin JSON payload is, as of the books append-only-evidence hook's design, used by every existing consumer (events-log-artifact.sh, validate-handoff-location.sh, validate-meta-write.sh, validate-plan-write.sh, validate-state-sync.sh, events-log-lifecycle.sh) only as event-logging provenance (passed through as --cwd to a recorder script) -- never to resolve a relative file_path or scope a git -C invocation. A hook needing to read a file's committed (HEAD) content from a possibly-relative file_path should join file_path onto cwd when not already absolute, then derive the repo root via `git -C "$(dirname "$ABS_FILE")" rev-parse --show-toplevel` rather than assuming cwd itself is the repo root -- no existing helper in this codebase does this yet.
